en: The Sūtra of the Greatly Powerful Vidyārāja Ucchuṣma, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ajitaśānti of North India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Homage to all Buddhas. Furthermore, O Bodhisattvas, at that time, within the assembly, there were immeasurable koṭis...
Surrounded by the vidyādhara sages,
Maheśvara, the Great King and Lord of the Mahābhūtas,
rose from his seat and prostrated himself with his head touching the ground.
First, he prostrated at the feet of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and spoke these words:
"O Bodhisattva, I pray that you will expound the teachings of great power,
which are unfailing and unimpeded."
One of incomparable strength and heroic vigor;
beloved by Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva;
and the one to whom all devas, asuras, Brahmā kings, and Śakras look up in reverence.
It is that which causes fear to yakṣas, rākṣasas, vighnas, and pūtanas;
it subdues enemies and accomplishes all tasks.
Regarding that which is secret in the maṇḍala ritual, at that time the assembly together praised Maheśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! Well-conceived! Excellent, excellent, O Great Lord of the Multitudes!"
"For the sake of those such as us, please grant your firm exhortation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
having gracefully brandished and cast his vajra, [spoke].
He then descended from his vajra-adorned lotus seat,
surveyed that assembly,
and immediately entered the samādhi of the Great Wrathful Joy of the Terrifying Vajra.
Thereafter, the immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of karmic obstructions for which they were destined were all utterly terrified;
they all saw their own bodies being suppressed and subdued by Ucchuṣma.
As their lives were about to end,
as if encountering the conflagration at the end of an eon, their minds became bewildered and distressed;
they all cried out with one voice, "We only pray that you will have compassion for us and grant us fearlessness."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi arose calmly from samādhi and addressed his assembly, saying:
O Greatly Majestic One, O Greatly Radiant One, O Greatly Wrathful One, it is as you have said.
Such is the Blessed One: the Greatly Majestic One, the Greatly Wrathful One, and the Greatly Radiant One.
At that time, the Bhagavān, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
turned his gaze like a lion and, looking about, spoke these words:
"O Lord of the Great Assembly, I shall now proclaim the secret maṇḍala rite of Ucchuṣma."
If one hears it even briefly, all undertakings will be fully accomplished;
there shall be no untimely or accidental deaths,
and no evil events whatsoever shall affect the person.
The Vināyakas shall find no opportunity to harm him;
he shall be loved and revered by all sentient beings,
and all enemies shall always remain far away from him.
All secret mantras shall attain accomplishment and efficacy;
all vajra dharmas shall be spontaneously fulfilled;
and all inauspiciousness shall be immediately liberated.
May all auspiciousness and blessings always provide protection.
If one recites this vidyā ten thousand times,
it is equivalent to ascending the altar and receiving full empowerment.
Once one has received the transmission from an enlightened master,
one should next set forth the characteristics of the Ucchuṣma Maṇḍala;
first, one ought to fully receive the Three Refuges and the Eight Precepts.
Having generated the bodhicitta with loving-kindness, wisdom, and compassion,
one should select a suitable location for establishing the mandala site,
whether it be in the mountains or in a village dwelling.
Whether in a wilderness or a cold forest,
in a pure chamber or on the bank of a river,
beneath a solitary tree or in a quiet house or shrine.
Construct the maṇḍala on ground prepared according to the rules,
measuring three cubits, four cubits, eight cubits, or even sixteen cubits.
For rites of subjugation, it should be three cubits and triangular in shape.
For rites of pacification or the subduing of calamities, construct [the mandala] four or eight cubits in size;
for rites of increase or for kings, construct it sixteen cubits in size.
Perform this on the eighth day of the dark fortnight.
Alternatively, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
empower clear water with the heart-mantra and sprinkle it upon the ground;
furthermore, rub a circular mandala with red sandalwood.
Spread auspicious grass and scatter red *akāraṇīra* flowers;
scatter fragrant ointments and various flowers upon the maṇḍala.
Empower one hundred and eight *khadira* stakes with mantras.
Drive stakes into the four corners and the center of the great mandala to establish the boundary of the site (*bhūmibandha*).
Then, perform the fundamental *sarvavikṣepa-mudrā* and recite the secret mantra seven times.
Take red sandalwood and smear it all over the ground.
Construct boundary lines using threads of five colors;
employ yellow, red, green, and black for the four corners and four gates.
Then, paint the Buddha at the center of the altar.
To the Buddha’s left is painted the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
holding a vajra;
he is accompanied by various messengers and the vidyā-snakes of the vajra-hook.
Holding a pestle, he gazes up at the Bodhisattva.
Next to his right is the Vidyārāja Ucchuṣma,
holding a blue *nanda*— in the language of Tang, a "club"— together with a host of yakṣas and asuras.
Together with Hārītī Mātṛ and her beloved sons as attendants,
they all gaze up at the Vidyārāja.
In the northeast corner, Maheśvara Deva holds a trident.
Together with his consort, Śakra,
the Lord of the Devas in the east, holds a vajra;
in the southeast corner, Agni, the God of Fire, holds a śakti.
In the south is Yama, holding a *nāṇaka*;
in the southwest is Nirṛti, holding a sword;
in the west is Varuṇa, holding a red noose.
In the northwest, Vāyu holds a crimson banner;
in the north, Vaiśravaṇa holds a gaṇa;
and on the three faces, the assembly of piśācas and nāgas is painted.
Inside the eastern gate, draw a trident for protection.
Fill new vases with pure water and precious items such as the five grains,
and wrap their necks with colored silk.
Take one mouth-vase and place it before the Buddha;
set a sandalwood pestle upon its opening.
All the other vases should have their openings stopped with red flowers or branches from fruit-bearing trees.
Place one flask at each of the four corners and at each of the four gates.
In front of the Buddha, place two sets of garments as offerings;
the Vajra-saṃgha and even the devas likewise use garments [for their offerings].
Before each image, place food, drink, incense, and flowers.
Outside the altar, on the path for the Brahma-conduct (brahmacarya), draw a square boundary and scatter ashes. First empower the vase one thousand and eight times, and then place it there.
Request the honored deities to act according to the Dharma;
then, lead the disciple in reciting the Vajrasamaya mantra,
ensuring that it is heard only by the disciple’s ears.
Wherever the scattered flowers land, that honored one possesses the karmic affinity for him; he shall receive the empowerment according to the Dharma.
If one ascends this maṇḍala, it is equivalent to having entered all maṇḍalas.
All celestial māras and vināyakas will be completely subdued and compliant.
Upon the end of life, one will be born in the palace of King Vaiśravaṇa, known as Aṇāvakānta.
Furthermore, the unsurpassed secret maṇḍala shall be explained again:
on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.
One may establish it upon a ground worthy of praise;
measuring four cubits with four gates and arrayed with five colors,
one should paint a Buddha within it using either bricks or lime powder.
Next to the right is Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
next to him is Hayagrīva Vidyārāja in a greatly wrathful form.
To the left of the Buddha is Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
To the left is the Great Powerful One, the Uṣṇīṣa Vidyārāja, in a form of great wrath.
Before the Buddha is Māmakī, the Mother of the Vajra Family.
At each of the four corners place a flask, and one flask before the Buddha.
Because it is covered with uncut silk brocade, it is named the "Victorious Vase.
In the northeast corner of the outer mandala,
Maheśvara, the Heavenly King, holds a trident together with his consort.
In the remaining corners, draw the seal of a half-mudgara or a full mudgara.
Offer worship with incense, flowers, food, and drink.
Then, according to the ritual, lead the disciples in for consecration.
The articles used are empowered by means of the heart-mantra of the Secret Mantra.
Furthermore, as for the mudrās:
the fundamental mudrā is the "all-pervading casting" mudrā.
First, stand upright and exert great effort to plant the left foot firmly on the ground.
Lean the body toward the left,
and with the right hand, grasp the thumb to form a fist.
Extend the arm and hold it upright.
Form a fist with the left hand and place it against the heart;
extend the index finger like a needle.
With the brows knit in a frown, one’s gaze should be focused.
This "Universal Casting Mudrā" is capable of terrifying all obstacles and difficulties;
it can also shatter the very bolts and pivots of the asura gates.
The Great Wrathful Mudrā:
With both hands, the middle fingers,
ring fingers, little fingers, and so forth are placed face-to-face with one another.
Pressing the three fingernails with the thumb,
one then clenches them into a fist;
extending the index finger, it is held together like a needle.
This mudrā is capable of performing all ritual activities:
binding, subduing, summoning, and expelling sudden obstacles;
furthermore, it causes one to remain far removed from those who would kill, from withered decay, and protects the body.
The Universal Flame Seal (Samantaprabhā-mudrā):
With the backs of the hands joined and the fingertips pointing downward,
it is called the "Lower-Joined Palms" (adhaḥ-saṃpuṭa).
Then, deeply interlace the fingers;
extend the two little fingers like needles and open the palms;
with the two thumbs, interlock them so that they press against the sides of the index finger nails.
This mudrā accomplishes all activities.
For the vajra-mudrā, interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward to form fists;
extend the middle finger and the index finger of the left hand.
The right middle finger and the left index finger are likewise.
The two middle fingers are joined together;
the tips of the index fingers are slightly bent, each positioned close to the side of its respective middle finger.
Place the two thumbs side by side, pressing against the sides of the ring fingers.
For the *checeng* (car-palms) seal, form a fist with the right hand while grasping the thumbs.
To form the *jiaodiao* (scissors) seal, follow the sequence of the preceding seal.
Extend the middle fingers like the blades of scissors and move them slowly.
For the Great Wall Courtyard Seal, form it as previously described for the Staff Seal.
Fully extend the two index fingers.
Form the *mūrdha-mudrā* (crown seal) as before at the great wall enclosure.
Bend the right index finger into the palm like the other fingers.
For the *mūrdha-mudrā*, form a large enclosure wall and insert the left index finger into it.
For the *kavaca-mudrā*, follow the enclosure wall;
bend the two index fingers so they touch each other like a ring.
This mudrā possesses great power and can accomplish all ritual activities.
Furthermore, regarding the method for painting the image:
use a piece of cotton cloth (kārpāsa) two cubits in both length and width.
Having settled the price through verbal agreement,
he then smeared the altar with cow dung and erected a hide within it.
One should make offerings of red flowers and food. Then,
having eaten, a skilled artisan should paint an image of the Tathāgata seated upon a lion throne,
with his hands in the gesture of preaching the Dharma (*dharmacakra-mudrā*), the thumb and index finger of the left hand joined together at their tips.
He extends his middle fingers, which are called the "small three-finger" measure, and does the same with his right hand.
Then, with his left hand, he turns the palm upward and places it horizontally across his heart.
Place the right wrist upon the tips of the little fingers and so forth of the left hand;
with the palms facing outward, spread the three fingers.
To the left of the Tathāgata, paint the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
The right hand holds a pestle, while the left hand forms the mudrā of inquiring about the Dharma; all five fingers are slightly bent, shaped like an inverted pan.
The arm is extended forward with the palm facing the Tathāgata.
To the left, paint the Great Powerful Vidyārāja Ucchuṣma in the form of a great wrathful deity;
his eyes are red and his entire body is dark blue-black.
His entire body blazes with flames and he has four arms;
his upper right hand holds a sword,
and the one below it holds a noose.
In the upper left, he holds a club;
below, a trident.
Flames rise from all his implements.
To the right of the Tathāgata was the Mother of the Vajra Family, Māmakī.
With abundant hair and a beautiful countenance, her entire body was a deep azure color.
Kneeling with palms joined in reverence, she addressed the Buddha.
The Mother of the Family stands to the right;
kneeling with both hands holding an incense burner, she makes offerings.
Her hide must not have been subjected to beating or defilement.
For those who are hairless,
do not use foul-smelling colors or colors derived from living beings.
The painters shall daily receive the Three Refuges and the Eight Precepts.
Maintaining a long-term fast and possessing a great mind of goodness, one should likewise wear clean new robes; the practitioner should not depart from their side.
It is best to achieve this quickly.
Hereafter, the same applies to painted images as well.
Furthermore, before this image,
facing east, recite the root mantra.
Beg for alms and observe silence, remaining as motionless as a withered tree.
When the printing of the base was completed,
and the sequence had thus reached six hundred thousand [recitations],
he then ascended the mountain and established the aforementioned secret maṇḍala.
Construct a great mandala while holding a sword.
Use agarwood and aloeswood as fuel for the fire;
burn saffron flowers mixed with white sandalwood throughout the day and night.
He shall become the foremost of the Vidyādhara sages, attaining all siddhis;
possessing great majestic power, his lifespan shall equal that of the sun and moon,
and at the end of his life, he will be reborn in the palace of Aṇākaravimāna.
If one places haridrā orpiment, or añjana eye-salve, or manaḥśilā realgar, or vermilion,
one should prepare a fire altar as previously described.
Its efficacy is like that of a sword.
If one performs the recitation without interruption for one month while begging for alms,
it shall be completed on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight.
On that day,

one should arrange the image and spread *aśvattha* leaves— abundant in the Guangfu region— before the image and perform the empowerment (*adhitiṣṭhati*) over three types of metal— gold, silver, and red copper— seven times.
Place it upon [the object] and maintain it through empowerment.
Flames shall arise, and its lifespan shall endure for an eon;
possessing great majestic power, all asuras, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ghosts, spirits, and devas will all be thoroughly subdued and brought into compliance.
If the month of empowerment for the three *kinnaras* is completed,
one should hold it as before while the flames arise;
this is the Greatly Powerful Vidyārāja, whose lifespan and body endure for an eon.
If a person holds three golden pestles,
with Dānava-jvālodbhava arising [therefrom],
their body becomes identical to that of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
If one substitutes three golden wheels for the vajra and flames arise,
one’s body will become radiant like the sun, and one will become a wheel-turning monarch among the vidyādharas.
Furthermore, if one abstains from food for three days...
On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should offer leaves of *pu-yang* (*Rhus chinensis*) and *ge-ta* (*Grewia asiatica*).
Before the image, one should arrange eight finger-widths of sand and iron hooks.
He performs the empowerment with his right hand over the leaf;
as flames arise, he grasps it and gazes penetratingly at the ground.
His status is equal to that of Śakra, sporting in the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
The devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits will show reverence and submission.
If one abstains from food for one day on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, [the results will be as follows].
Pūṣpa said: "One should place seven leaves from a *śrīparṇī* tree before the image, place realgar upon them, and empower it.
When flames arise, the vidyādhara should smear himself with it."
When smoke appears,
perform warm and virtuous practices;
if one recites [the mantra] one hundred thousand times on a mountain peak, [success will be attained].
The Greatly Powerful Vajravega, King of Radiance, appears;
though he is most terrifying, do not fear him with a distracted mind.
Speak what you must have done.
The Bhagavat accomplishes all tasks.
He merely requests a single boon from the vidyādhara sages;
whether to subdue asuras or to summon the devas, he does so entirely according to his will.
If one arranges the image at the auspicious entrance and completes three hundred thousand recitations,
an asura maiden will personally come out to welcome them.
Five hundred people may enter together;
those who create obstacles will find their bodies withered and dried up.
Furthermore, there is the method for painting images.
Take two cubits of silk cloth and paint the Great Powerful King Ucchuṣma.
His body is red in color and he has an enraged form with bared dog-teeth.
His eyes are narrow like those of a wildcat, and his yellow hair stands upright.
Holding a vajra in the left hand and a nāṇa in the right,
whether the practitioner eats or does not eat, and regardless of whether the food is pure or impure,
if one recites [the mantra] three hundred thousand times before the image, all that is undertaken will be accomplished.
If at the auspicious entrance,
the image is arranged facing north,
the practitioner faces south.
Construct a fire altar using well-seasoned firewood.
Offer powdered poison, mustard seeds, and one's own blood;
when these have been offered a full one thousand and eight times, the bodies of the asura women will be like those consumed by fire.
They presented the elixir of longevity and the transformative medicines.
Those who did not accept the medicines,
all the women took each other by the hand and entered the palace together.
"Since there was previously one who possessed clarity, I shall become king over him;
I do not fear the karma of Nārāyaṇa,
for his wheel-like lifespan lasts for many kalpas."
One will possess a noble and blissful body, radiating light;
through various miraculous transformations, one will be reborn in the heavens after death.
If this image is displayed at the auspicious entrance of a gate, [these benefits shall follow].
Construct a fire altar and burn *śīrṣapuṣpa* flowers;
when one thousand and eight have been completed over three days,
then perform the root *vyāpakamudrā*.
That gate will open immediately, and one may enter without obstruction.
If there is a dragon’s bank or a place where images are arrayed,
construct a fire altar and burn salt one thousand and eight times.
The dragon emerges to receive its mandate and may be dispatched at will.
If one has first fasted for three days,
one should place the image and the inscription upon a pyre made of *chái* (in the Tang language, *gǒuqǐ*) and construct a fire altar.
If one performs one thousand and eight recitations with mustard oil and mustard seeds,
one can summon all humans and devas.
If one forms a *siddhili* image using salt...
Construct a fire altar and cut the [substance] into pieces,
offering them into the fire three times each day for a full seven days.
By reciting the name [of the person], they will arrive from within a range of one hundred *yojana*.
If one arranges images within an empty temple or shrine,
constructs a fire altar using *aśvattha* wood,
and uses *kaṭphala* leaves mixed with mustard oil.
Recite it one thousand and eight times during each of the three periods of the day.
After seven days have passed, a celestial deity will appear and say, "What task shall I perform? Command me as you wish."
If one has first fasted for three days,
on the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
[one should perform the rite] before a śrīphala fruit in front of the Great Lord Maheśvara.
Covering [the object] with the right hand while performing the empowerment,
after a short while a great sound will arise;
the three Heavenly Kings will appear and receive your commands.

Spread out an image and construct a fire altar.

He struck the yakṣī on the knee,
whereupon she immediately showed him respect.

They all obeyed his command.
If one fashions a three-pronged trident from khadira wood and abstains from food for three days during a solar or lunar eclipse, [one shall achieve success].
Arrange images within a cemetery and make extensive offerings of incense, flowers, food, and drink. Then,
holding a trident in the right hand, perform the empowerment.

Śeṣaru-dhanvayāsa: this is the name of a medicinal herb, reddish-black in color, resembling gold, and produced in India.

If one sees [the deity] appearing within the sun, this is the true [manifestation]; place it before the image and perform empowerment (*adhitiṣṭhati*).

through reverence, smoke will arise and the form will vanish.

one takes a corpse without scars from a cold forest cemetery and bathes it with fragrant water.

one should make offerings of incense and flowers.

Sitting upon the heart of the corpse,
take a pure white skull and fill it completely with white mustard seeds.

the mustard seeds will all vanish.

one can raise the dead and overcome formidable enemies.

The Fundamental Seal of the Bhagavān:
First, place the backs of the hands together and interlace the fingers;
the little fingers and thumbs should join with one another like needles.

For the Root Mudrā, beckon both thumbs together.

For the scissors mudrā (*kartarīmudrā*), first place the two hands side by side.
Bend the little fingers and press the thumbs over the nails so that they form a ring.
Then, forming two circles, they are grasped together;
the index and middle fingers are extended side by side,
with the right middle finger pressing against the side of the left index finger.
Forming the shape of the two blades of a pair of scissors,
slowly move the blades and rotate them to the right three times while reciting the secret mantra; thus the boundary is established.
If one circumambulates three times to the left, the boundary is dissolved.
For this, use the Great Mind Mantra.
As for the *saṃsthāpana-mudrā*: form a fist with the right hand and extend the thumb straight upward.
If there are those who are wrathful,
one should subdue them with the mudrā while reciting the mantra;

For the staff mudrā (*daṇḍamudrā*): with both hands, press the thumbs against the middle joints of the ring fingers to form two rings;
grasp these two rings together with great force.
Extend the index fingers like needles and employ the Great Heart Mantra (*mahāhṛdaya-mantra*).
Next is the Head Mudrā, which follows the previous Staff Mudrā:
extend both index fingers and bend their middle joints,
then touch the tips of the heads together.
The crown mudrā is as before;
extend the two index fingers and employ the Great Heart Mantra.
The fingernail mudrā follows the previous crown mudrā.
Bend each index finger to form the seal at five locations; this is identical to donning the armor.
For the wall-and-enclosure seal, follow the previous armor seal by extending both index fingers;
this is identical to surrounding oneself with a wall and enclosure.
For the Hook Seal (*aṅkuśamudrā*), as before, bend both index fingers like hooks and slowly beckon with them.
This seal is used for summoning the two-footed and four-footed classes [of beings] by means of the Great Heart Mantra (*mahāhṛdayamantra*).
The *bhīṣaṇamudrā* is like the *aṅkuśamudrā*, with the middle finger of the left hand extended.
It is used to cause all malevolent spirits (*bhūta-graha*) to tremble with fear; employ the *mahācittamantra*.
Next is the *uṣṇīṣamudrā*: as in the preceding *bhīṣaṇamudrā*, the two index fingers are crossed and inserted into the palms.
The middle fingers of both hands are slightly bent at their first joints, with the tips touching one another.
This mudrā is used when reciting [the mantra];
it can subdue those who are difficult to tame by employing the Heart of the Heart Mantra.
For the Universal Flame Seal (Samantaprabhā-mudrā), extend the fingers outward.
Join the little fingers together like needles.
Slightly bend the thumbs and each grasp the side of the nail of the index finger.
Slightly raise the remaining fingers in the shape of a flame.

then extend the left middle finger.
With the right index finger extended like a needle, employ the Great Heart Mantra.
Form the "chariot-staff" mudrā with the right hand by making a fist with the thumb tucked inside.

If one offers powdered black pepper and long pepper, [the same result follows].
If one recites the *rāṇa* one thousand and eight times amidst the fire of a cremation ground (*śmaśāna*) or the fire of a *caṇḍāla*’s house,
all *gaṇas* will be honored. If one recites it one thousand and eight times amidst the fire of withered flower garlands offered to women, all *gaṇas* will be honored.
If one consecrates either *gorocanā* or *manaḥśilā* one thousand and eight times and anoints the body,
wicked people will hold one in high esteem, and one will be spared from weapons when entering battle.
If one wishes to subdue an enemy, one should place *svaludantana* before them.
Alternatively, one may empower cow bezoar over *aśvattha* leaves one thousand and eight times and apply it to the eyes;
those who see this will hold one in high esteem and respect, which brings about supreme benefits.
If one takes barley and dragon-flower filaments (*nāgakesara*) and offers them into the fire one thousand and eight times, men will hold one in high esteem and respect.
Furthermore, regardless of whether one is pure or impure, if one recites [the mantra] three hundred thousand times, [the same result shall be attained].
Mix black sesame seeds with clarified butter and offer them into the fire one thousand and eight times; the efficacy will be attained.
Alternatively, fashion an image of that person out of salt.
Cutting from the right foot, one offers it into the fire until it is exhausted;
this brings about the honor and respect of men.
If mustard seeds are mixed with its oil, [the same result follows].
If one recites [the mantra] one thousand and eight times over fire, kings, ministers, and nobles will hold one in high esteem.
If one consecrates flowers, fruits, or incense seven times and presents them to others, they will hold one in high esteem.
If one consecrates eye salve and applies it, those who see it will hold one in high esteem.
If one offers *kaṭphala* leaves into the fire one thousand and eight times, it is for *uḍaḍhāna*.
If one offers sesame seeds into the fire one thousand and eight times, it is for *vināśana*.
If one recites the mantra Ucconana one thousand and eight times over ashes from a cremation ground mixed with water while fire is advancing,
or if one cuts *kūṭaka* and mixes it with oil;
Recite the mantra *uccāṭana* one thousand and eight times over fire;
if the garment is wet with water, wear it while standing in the sun.
Recite the secret mantra until the garment is dry, then walk upon sand.
If one performs the empowerment of the mantra *Māraṇī* while covering a stone mound with the hand in a temple of the Lord of the Heaven of Sovereignty (*Īśvara*),
or if one holds the secret mantra before the noble Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
Furthermore, snap your fingers without ceasing, O Ma-ra-ning.
If you encounter an enemy,
first recite the secret mantra, then utter "Hūṃ" or "Phaṭ."
He will lose his mind or have his head shattered.

On the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,
perform one thousand and eight empowerments before an image of Vajrapāṇi.
As for the medicinal substances, they will produce the sound "khaṭa khaṭa."
Holding the form within the mouth, one shall live for a thousand years.

If one takes the blood from one's own body and mixes it with mustard seeds,

If one offers clarified butter into a bowl, the moon will again appear;
by anointing one's eyes, one's form is concealed and one lives for a thousand years.
If one recites this ten thousand times, that person will become like a servant.
To cause Māraṇī also to act according to one’s will, the secret mantra is as follows:
*Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Oṃ vajrakurudha mahāmāla hana daha paca vidhvaṃsaya ucchuṣmakurudha hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. Next is the method for painting the image.
Using a piece of cloth the size of one cubit,
paint the Great Powerful Vidyārāja,
his entire body black and his canine fangs bared.
His yellow hair shoots upward;
in his wrath, flames arise from his entire body.
He holds a vajra in his left hand and hurls a *nāga* with his right.
On the eighth or fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should display the image and make offerings of red flowers, red food, and drink.

One should empower realgar and a new piece of leather; using a cord made from divine thread (*devasūtra*)—woven by a pure practitioner of India from leather threads into a continuous rope as thick as three fingers—one should bind it around the shoulder. Alternatively, one may use items such as wooden sandals, pestles, wheels, halberds, axes, or swords.
If flames arise, one achieves the status of a vidyādhara;
if smoke is produced, one gains the power of invisibility;
and if heat is generated, one should perform virtuous deeds.
Furthermore, the protective mantra of the Great Powerful Vidyārāja is as follows:

Namaḥ ratnatrayāya | Namaḥ śrīvajrapāṇaye | Mahāyakṣasenāpate | Tadyathā | Oṃ vajrakrodha mahāmāra hana daha paca matha vikiraṇavidhvamsaya ucchuṣmakrodha hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā | If one fills a pure vessel with cow’s milk...
Empower a single flower and cast it into [the vessel]; when this is completed twenty-one times, the efficacy will be realized.
Furthermore, as for the method of the visualization gate:
support the forehead with the fingers.
Visualize:
the syllable Oṃ is in the center, red in color;
next, place it at the heart.
The syllable HŪṂ is in the center, colored blue;
it rests upon the heels.
The syllable PHAṬ is in the center, colored pure white.
Visualize oneself as identical to the deity and recite the protective mantra twenty-one times; wherever one goes according to one's will,
it shall be established as a boundary.
One achieves protection so that the hosts of Māras do not approach;
when about to sleep, one’s dreams become pure.
This three-syllable visualization gate is also applicable for use during the recitation of all Vajra families.
